name: Chicken Korma
cuisine: Mughlai / North Indian (Awadhi–Delhi–Hyderabadi court cooking; common on Mumbai's Mughlai and Muslim-restaurant menus)

ingredients.name: Curd (dahi), whole-milk
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ cup (30 g for the marinade, 30 g for the gravy paste)

ingredients.name: Salt (namak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp in total (¼ tsp in the marinade, ¼ tsp in the gravy)

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: 60 ml (¼ cup) for blending + 90 ml (⅓ cup + 1 tbsp) for simmering; plus 3 tbsp hot water for soaking the nuts (drained, not counted)

equipment: Mixing bowl with a lid or plate, for marinating
Small bowl, for soaking the nuts
Heavy-bottomed kadai or small saucepan (about 18–20 cm) with a lid
Slotted spoon, for lifting the onions out
Mixer-grinder with a small chutney jar
Measuring spoons and a ¼-cup measure

steps.title: Pat the chicken dry
steps.text: Pat the 200 g chicken curry-cut pieces dry with paper towel. Make 1 shallow cut on each large piece.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, board and knife with soap after handling raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: Matte, not wet, surface; small cuts on the bigger pieces
steps.videoShot: A paper towel pressing on the chicken pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: In the mixing bowl, put 30 g (2 tbsp) curd, 1 tsp (5 g) ginger paste, 1 tsp (5 g) garlic paste, ½ tsp (1 g) Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp (2 g) coriander powder, a small pinch of turmeric and ¼ tsp (about 1.25 g) salt. Mix smooth.
steps.visualCue: An even, pale orange paste with no lumps of curd
steps.videoShot: Powders falling onto white curd and being stirred in.

steps.title: Coat and rest the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken, turn it until every piece is coated, cover, and leave in the fridge.
steps.visualCue: Every piece evenly coated
steps.cameraCheck: The coated chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A spoon turning the chicken in the marinade.

steps.title: Soak the nuts
steps.text: Put 6 cashews (8 g) and 3 almonds (4 g) in a small bowl and cover with 3 tbsp hot water.
steps.tip: Want a whiter, smoother gravy? Slip the skins off the almonds after soaking; it is optional.
steps.visualCue: The nuts look plump and a shade paler
steps.videoShot: Hot water being poured over the nuts.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Peel the 80 g onion, halve it, and slice it into thin, even half-moons (about 2 mm).
steps.tip: Even slices brown evenly; thick and thin pieces together give a mix of burnt and raw.
steps.visualCue: Thin slices of the same thickness, separated into strands
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced onion on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife slicing thin half-moons.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put 2 tsp (10 ml) oil in the kadai on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily when you tilt the pan
steps.videoShot: Oil being poured into the kadai.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and spread it out. Cook, stirring every 30–60 seconds; lower the heat to low-medium once the edges start to colour.
steps.tip: The last 2 minutes go from golden to burnt very fast. If any pieces turn black, pick them out; burnt onion makes the gravy bitter.
steps.visualCue: Evenly deep golden-brown (the colour of strong tea), shrunken and slightly crisp at the edges; a sweet, toasty smell, no black bits
steps.cameraCheck: The browned onions in the kadai
steps.videoShot: The spatula stirring golden-brown onion strands.

steps.title: Lift out the onion
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Lift the onions out with the slotted spoon onto a plate, leaving the oil in the kadai.
steps.visualCue: Onions on the plate, a thin film of oil left in the kadai
steps.videoShot: The slotted spoon lifting out the onions.

steps.title: Cool the onion
steps.text: Spread them out and let them cool.
steps.visualCue: Warm, no longer steaming
steps.videoShot: Steam rising off the onions, then stopping.

steps.title: Blend the gravy paste
steps.text: Drain the nuts. Put the onions, nuts, the remaining 30 g (2 tbsp) curd and 60 ml (¼ cup) water in the small mixer jar. Blend to a smooth paste.
steps.tip: Blending the curd with the nuts and onion, rather than adding it plain later, makes it much less likely to split.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, light-brown paste with no visible nut bits when rubbed between two fingers
steps.videoShot: The jar lid opening on a smooth beige-brown paste.

steps.title: Heat the ghee
steps.text: Add 1 tsp (5 g) ghee to the oil left in the kadai and put it on low-medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The ghee melts and mixes with the oil
steps.videoShot: A spoon of ghee melting in the kadai.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add the bay leaf, 2 cracked cardamom pods, 2 cloves and the 2 cm cinnamon.
steps.visualCue: The spices sizzle gently, the cloves swell, and a warm, sweet smell rises
steps.videoShot: Whole spices hitting the ghee and sizzling.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken with all its marinade. Raise the heat to medium and cook, turning the pieces every minute.
steps.visualCue: The chicken turns opaque white on the outside and the marinade thickens and sticks lightly to the pieces
steps.videoShot: The spatula turning the chicken pieces.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Lower the heat to low-medium, cover, and cook, stirring once halfway.
steps.visualCue: The chicken releases its juices and the masala looks loose and wet; fat starts to show at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: Lifting the lid to show the chicken in its juices.

steps.title: Add the paste off the heat
steps.text: Turn off the heat and wait 1 minute. Pour in the onion-nut-curd paste and stir it through.
steps.tip: Adding curd to a very hot pan is the main reason korma splits. The 1-minute pause is enough.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, evenly brown gravy coating the chicken, no white streaks
steps.videoShot: Paste being poured over the chicken and stirred in.

steps.title: Cook the paste
steps.text: Put the kadai back on low heat and cook, stirring often so it does not catch.
steps.visualCue: The gravy darkens a shade, thickens, and small beads of fat appear at the edges; the raw-onion smell is gone
steps.cameraCheck: Fat at the edges of the gravy
steps.videoShot: The spatula pulling the gravy back to show fat seeping at the edge.

steps.title: Add water and the rest of the salt
steps.text: Add 90 ml (⅓ cup + 1 tbsp) water and the remaining ¼ tsp (about 1.25 g) salt. Stir and scrape the bottom.
steps.visualCue: A pourable, smooth gravy
steps.videoShot: Water swirling into the brown gravy.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Bring to a gentle bubble, cover, and simmer on low, stirring every 4–5 min.
steps.visualCue: Lazy bubbles, the gravy thickens to coat the back of a spoon, and the chicken is tender when pressed
steps.videoShot: Slow bubbles breaking on the surface of the korma.

steps.title: Check it is cooked
steps.text: Insert a thermometer into the thickest piece near the bone, or cut into it.
steps.tip: Still pink? Simmer 3–4 min more and check again.
steps.visualCue: 74 °C (165 °F) or above; white at the bone, juices clear, no pink
steps.cameraCheck: The cut-open thickest piece, or the thermometer reading
steps.videoShot: A knife opening the thickest piece at the bone.

steps.title: Adjust the consistency
steps.text: Too thick? Add 1–2 tbsp hot water. Too thin? Simmer uncovered 2–3 min. Taste and add a pinch of salt only if needed.
steps.visualCue: A medium-thick gravy that coats the chicken and slowly runs off a spoon
steps.videoShot: Gravy dripping slowly off a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with garam masala
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp (0.5 g) garam masala (and 2 drops kewra water, if using). Stir gently and switch off the heat.
steps.visualCue: A fragrant, glossy gravy
steps.cameraCheck: The garam masala on the gravy
steps.videoShot: A pinch of garam masala falling on the korma.

steps.title: Rest (dum)
steps.text: Keep the lid on and leave the korma to rest off the heat.
steps.tip: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon and cloves before serving if you like; they are not eaten.
steps.visualCue: A thin layer of fat rises to the surface; the gravy settles
steps.videoShot: The lid going on, then lifting to show glossy korma.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Transfer to a bowl and scatter 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves on top.
steps.visualCue: Brown-beige, glossy gravy with green flecks on top
steps.videoShot: Coriander falling onto the korma in a bowl.

reasons: a good protein dose (about 36 g) with no deep-frying, no cream, no sugar and real nuts (healthy fats, magnesium, vitamin E), but korma is a rich gravy by design: about 30 g fat, 8.6 g saturated (ghee, curd, chicken), about 1,130 mg sodium and very little fibre or vegetables. Restaurant versions usually add cream, more ghee or oil, deep-fried birista and sometimes sugar, which can push a bowl well past 600 kcal with double the saturated fat.

researchRating.basis: a classic of Mughlai cooking and one of the most widely known Indian curries worldwide; The Wanderlust Kitchen's chicken korma shows 4.5/5 from 1,332 votes and Rouxbe reports a 95% success rating; Swiggy's Mumbai chicken, chicken-curry and Mughlai pages list chicken korma among popular dishes, and many Mumbai Mughlai and Irani-Muslim restaurants carry it. Small deduction because "korma" means very different things (rich Mughlai braise versus mild, sweet, creamy restaurant curry), so expectations and reviews vary, and home versions can split or turn bitter if the onions burn.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 3 days; cool it within 1 hour of cooking. Freezer: up to 2 months; the gravy may look slightly grainy after thawing, which a good stir while reheating fixes. Reheat in a covered pan on low heat with 2–3 tbsp water for 5–6 min, stirring, until piping hot to the bone; avoid boiling hard, which can split the curd. Microwave: covered, 2–3 min, stirring halfway.
leftoverRemix: korma chicken roll (FitPlate twist on the Mumbai kathi roll). Pull the chicken off the bone and shred it. Simmer it in the leftover gravy, uncovered, until thick and almost dry (3–4 min). Spread on a warm paratha or roti, add sliced onion, a squeeze of lemon, a little green chutney and coriander, then roll it up. A mild, nutty filling that works cold for a lunchbox too.
burnOff: about 7.0 km of running (490 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 9.8 km of brisk walking (about 2 hours at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 670 kcal, est.), about 9.6 km of running.

navratri.reason: contains chicken, onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided in the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains chicken, onion and garlic, avoided under the common Ekadashi rule set (same as Navratri in the sources used).

jain.reason: contains chicken plus onion, garlic and ginger (root vegetables).

ramadan.reason: use halal chicken; a classic, filling iftar or dinner curry with good protein, but rich (about 30 g fat, est.) and salty (about 1,130 mg sodium, est.) for sehri unless you cut the salt and oil.

jain.reason: contains chicken, plus onion, garlic and ginger (root vegetables).

sattvik.reason: contains chicken, and onion and garlic are the base of the gravy.

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or besan, and no hing (asafoetida) used; check the label of packaged garam masala, which can contain hing compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: the gravy uses curd and ghee; use the Dairy-free variant in section 4 (coconut yoghurt or cashew cream, oil instead of ghee).

description: A non-veg (chicken), gluten-free Mughlai curry in a browned-onion, curd and cashew-almond gravy; dairy-free, vegetarian (paneer or navratan korma) and low-oil versions below.

variants.reason: Jain diet excludes meat, and the gravy is built on onion and garlic. The vegetarian korma route is the Vegetarian variant below; a Jain version of navratan korma (no onion, garlic, ginger or root vegetables) belongs to FitPlate dish 78 (Navratan Korma), where it will be researched.
the dish is defined by chicken. The plant-based route is the Vegetarian variant (navratan/vegetable korma) made with the Dairy-free swaps below (coconut yoghurt or cashew cream, oil instead of ghee).
main recipe already gluten-free (no flour, no hing). Check the label of packaged garam masala.
